exercise.name: Cable Y-Raise
library_steps: Stand between two low pulleys, holding each handle in the opposite hand.
Raise your arms up and out into a wide Y above your head.
exercise.one_line_summary: Standing between two low pulleys, each hand holding the handle from the other side so the cables cross in front of the hips; nearly straight arms rise from in front of the thighs up and out into a wide Y overhead. Side delts do the main work, the rear delts and trapezius help.

setup.target: Both low (0.1-0.3 m), a little in front of the body.
Opposite hand to each cable; thumbs up/back at the top.

movement.measure: arm raised from hanging, in the scapular plane (~30 deg forward of the side)

muscles.emg: Side delt works hardest when the arm is raised out to the side (S3).
muscles.role: Raises the arm out and up; library primary.

muscles.emg: Active in raises with the arm turned (S3).
muscles.role: Helps raise the arm; library secondary.

muscles.emg: The overhead Y raise is the reference lower-trapezius exercise (S1, S2); upper trapezius also works (S1).
muscles.role: Rotates the shoulder blade up; library secondary.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Hands go straight up, not out.
mistakes.why_it_matters: The Y is ~30 deg out from vertical.

sources.citation: Garcia JF, Herrera C, Maciukiewicz JM, et al. 2023. Variation of muscle recruitment during exercises performed below horizontal arm elevation that target the lower trapezius. J Electromyogr Kinesiol 70:102777.
sources.what_it_gave: The prone 'Y' (arms raised overhead in a Y) is the gold-standard lower-trapezius exercise; upper trapezius also works.

sources.citation: Ekstrom RA, Donatelli RA, Soderberg GL. 2003. Surface electromyographic analysis of exercises for the trapezius and serratus anterior muscles. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 33(5):247-258.
sources.what_it_gave: 10 exercises, 30 subjects: the shrug gave the highest upper-trapezius EMG; shoulder horizontal extension (arm moving back at shoulder height) the highest middle trapezius; the prone overhead raise in a Y the highest lower trapezius.

sources.citation: Coratella G, Tornatore G, Longo S, Esposito F, Ce E. 2020. An electromyographic analysis of lateral raise variations and frontal raise in competitive bodybuilders. Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(17):6015.
sources.what_it_gave: Lateral raise variants vs frontal raise: frontal raise mainly works the front delt (with pectoralis major more than any lateral raise); lateral raise with a neutral humerus works the side delt most; internal rotation shifts work to the rear delt and upper trapezius.

clip_check.check: Start: hands in front of the thighs, cables crossing
End: arms in a wide Y overhead
Both fists closed on the handles; cables cross in front, clear of the body
Side delts strongest red, traps and rear delts light
